decision.confidence: moderate-high on direction and rough size; CPU-only, one dataset, 120 queries, sentence-transformers path
decision.rationale: nomic beats the current BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 default on every retrieval metric on the same 120 queries and same memory units: recall@10 0.681 vs 0.571 (delta +0.110, bootstrap 95% CI +0.051..+0.173), MRR 0.545 vs 0.438 (+0.107, CI +0.042..+0.174), recall@1 +0.081 (CI +0.010..+0.156), nDCG@10 +0.104 (CI +0.053..+0.156). All CIs exclude zero and the sign is consistent across metrics, categories and both hit@k-style metrics. Cost: ~3.6x index build time, exactly 2x index storage per unit, ~2.2x single-query latency p50 (68.5 vs 31.7 ms, noisy), ~2.2x model RSS in the ST path, 4.1x weight file size; all within the engine's CPU-only operating envelope for a full reindex.
conditions: MNEMOSYNE_EMBEDDING_DIM=768 must be set (engine dim map has no nomic entry and falls back to 384)
MNEMOSYNE_EMBEDDING_QUERY_PREFIX='search_query: ' and MNEMOSYNE_EMBEDDING_DOC_PREFIX='search_document: ' must be set (engine applies no built-in nomic prefixes; these numbers assume them)
full reindex required: 384 -> 768 dim is a hard schema change (sqlite-vec tables recreated at the new dim)
validate engine-native fastembed ONNX quality before rollout; this benchmark measured the sentence-transformers PyTorch path, engine uses fastembed ONNX
decision.not_pending_because: the measurement succeeded; F1/BLEU/LLM-judge are blocked (marked BLOCKED) but are downstream QA metrics, not embedding-retrieval metrics, and the decision to reindex rests on retrieval quality + cost, which were measured.

protocol.label: MemBase LoCoMo loader + NaiveRAG message-unit contract (custom harness; not the official 3-stage runner)
protocol.dataset: LoCoMo (snap-research/locomo data/locomo10.json, 10 conversations, 272 sessions, 5,882 messages, 1,986 QA pairs)

subset.selection_rule: first N trajectories in loader order; first 30 valid QA pairs per trajectory (QA with >=1 evidence id resolved against that trajectory's messages)

protocol.memory_unit: one LoCoMo message per unit, serialized exactly as MemBase NaiveRAGLayer.add_message: 'Speaker {name} (role: {role}) says: {content}\nTimestamp: {iso}'
protocol.retrieval: dense cosine top-10 over all units of the same trajectory (per-user index); gold = LoCoMo evidence dia_ids prefixed by the MemBase loader as 'U<sample>:<dia_id>'
protocol.metrics: recall@1/5/10 = |gold ∩ top_k| / |gold|; MRR = 1/rank of first relevant; nDCG@10 with binary relevance

prefixes.bge_small: Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages:
prefixes.rationale: each model is used per its own model card (bge query instruction; nomic search_document:/search_query: task prefixes)

protocol.warmup: first 5 queries excluded from latency stats; model files pre-cached before measured load
protocol.not_official_runner: MemBase's stage-2 SearchRunner loads stage-1 .pkl dumps and returns memory contents without unit ids, so gold-evidence scoring is not possible from its output; this harness reuses the official dataset loader and the exact NaiveRAG unit serialization/granularity instead.

headline.why_not_pending: 120 paired queries; every delta CI excludes zero; effect size ~10x the CI half-width is not required because sign-consistency holds across recall@1/5/10, MRR and nDCG@10, and per-category deltas are non-negative.

scale_notes.index_build: measured 2,080 units: 57.3 s (36.3 units/s) vs 208.5 s (10.0 units/s); linear in unit count, so a 100k-unit DB is ~46 min vs ~2.8 h single-threaded CPU
scale_notes.index_storage: float32 N x dim x 4: 1,536 B/unit (384d) vs 3,072 B/unit (768d); production stores that quantize to int8 could halve both
scale_notes.query_latency: p50 31.7 ms vs 68.5 ms per query (encode + cosine over <=663 units); grows with DB size for the cosine scan, but the engine uses sqlite-vec for the real store
scale_notes.rss: sentence-transformers peak 743 MB (bge) vs 1,666 MB (nomic); engine fastembed ONNX is expected to be lower but was not measured

performance.context_tokens_note: Memory units and the tiktoken cl100k_base tokenizer are identical for both models; per-query top-10 context totals differ only because the retrieved top-10 sets differ (nomic 586.5 vs bge-small 545.9 mean cl100k tokens/query). No model-specific tokenizer is involved.
performance.note_on_noise: Quality metrics are deterministic given the fixed 120-query subset; their CIs are bootstrap over queries (sampling noise, 10k resamples). Index-build and query-latency timings were taken while other agent jobs (node/pytest) shared the 8 logical cores, and the bge-small run overlapped more contention than the nomic run (bge p95 93.1 ms vs nomic p95 81.4 ms is confounded; p50 31.7 vs 68.5 ms is the more stable signal). Re-measure latency on an idle machine before quoting absolute numbers.
performance.index_footprint_basis: N x dim x 4 bytes (npy) + id list; measured from the saved index files

not_measured.reason: the engine (mnemosyne 3.15.x) embeds through fastembed 0.8.0 ONNX, not sentence-transformers. This benchmark uses sentence-transformers (the loading path named in the workstream brief). fastembed 0.8.0 lists both models in TextEmbedding.list_supported_models() (bge-small 384d / 0.067 GB; nomic 768d / 0.52 GB), so the engine can load both, but ONNX-converted weights can differ slightly from the PyTorch weights measured here.

reindex_implication.engine_backend: fastembed 0.8.0 in the Hermes venv supports nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5 (768d) and BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 (384d); engine dim map falls back to 384 for nomic, so MNEMOSYNE_EMBEDDING_DIM=768 is mandatory
reindex_implication.dims_change: 384 -> 768, so a full reindex is mandatory; stale 384d vectors would break similarity search (checked at store/search time)
reindex_implication.cost: re-embeds every memory unit once; index storage doubles per unit (3,072 vs 1,536 bytes/unit float32)
